# deps/young-package

New dependency or version published too recently.

A package added to package.json that was first published less than packages.minAgeDays ago (default 7), or a new dependency version published less than packages.minReleaseAgeHours ago (default 48). Looked up with --online, packages.online, or `ubon vet`.

- Default level: `block`.
- Levels: The package install check in hooks returns "ask" instead of blocking, so a person decides. Names and scopes on packages.allow are not checked.
- Looks at: what the change did, comparing each file before and after.
- References: [CWE-1357](https://cwe.mitre.org/data/definitions/1357.html), [CWE-829](https://cwe.mitre.org/data/definitions/829.html), OWASP A03:2025.

## Why it matters

Most malicious packages and hijacked versions are found and removed within hours or days of publication. A short cooldown keeps them out of the project while that happens.

## Not flagged

- next 15.1.2: a new version; its publish date needs a registry lookup, which is off in this run
- typescript@next: a dist-tag that usually points at a nightly build; offline it is listed under not checked
- brand-new-helper: a new package whose first publish date needs a lookup
- react: unchanged
- no finding is ever reported from a guess: without lookups the rule only says what it did not check

## How to fix

Pin a version published before the cooldown, or wait; a person can add the package to packages.allow in ubon.json.

## If the finding is wrong

Add a comment on the line above, in the comment syntax of the file, that says who decided and why:

```
ubon-ignore deps/young-package: <who decided>: <evidence>
```

Or turn the rule off for the project in `ubon.json`: `"rules": { "deps/young-package": "off" }`. See [configuration](../../config.md).
